newsitem.title: USA: U.S. warns Belgrade not to crush peaceful protests. [CORRECTED 10:07 GMT 3/12]
newsitem.headline: U.S. warns Belgrade not to crush peaceful protests. [CORRECTED 10:07 GMT 3/12]

text.p: The United States warned Serbia on Monday it would react with outrage against any use of force against anti-government protesters who Washington says are demonstrating peacefully over alleged vote-rigging.
The State Department also said it had sent a "very stiff message" to Belgrade that it should give up attempts to re-run municipal elections it lost last month.
Belgrade has been shaken by two weeks of street protests since the government annulled an opposition victory in local polls on Nov. 17.
The demonstrators have demanded an end to President Slobodan Milosevic's nine-year rule. Milosevic has threatened to use force to quell the protests.

"Our government has made it perfectly clear publicly and privately to the Serbian authorities at every level, and with a variety of different individuals who are responsible for public order and for security, that the United States would be outraged if any attempt was made to use force against the demonstrators," a State Department spokesman said.
"The demonstrators have a right to be on the streets of Belgrade to express their views peacefully, as they are currently doing," spokesman Nicholas Burns said.
"We just hope that this situation can continue to be relatively peaceful, as it has been so far," he added.
Burns said the decision by the Milosevic government to annul the Nov. 17 election results and carry out new "sham elections" was "an outrage against international norms".
He said U.S. charge d'affaires Richard Miles had given Milosevic and other officials "a very stiff message ... that the Serbian government ought to respect the rights of the Serbian people.
"The results of the municipal elections ought to be respected, some way must be found by the government to walk back from its decision to stifle those elections," he said.

Burns also attacked attempts by Serbian authorities to suppress reporting of the demonstrations and said U.S. officials had protested to Belgrade over the arrest of journalists of the independent newspaper Blitz.

The U.S. spokesman repeated earlier warnings that an "outer wall" of sanctions against the rump Yugoslavia -- Serbia and Montenegro -- blocking its access to international financial institutions, would be maintained partly because of the handling of the elections.
